title: v1/chat: output-contract negotiator + fncall handoff buffering for streaming parity
author: Maya Chen
commits: 5a9d7c7: add output contract negotiator module and unit tests
b3ef2a1: integrate negotiator into v1/chat adapter path
c0f9a11: implement fncall streaming handoff buffer and heartbeat
d4e3b2f: update adapter integration tests and compatibility fixtures
e7c5d44: docs: add migration note and examples for stop/logprob mapping
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat behavior closer to OpenAI chat.completions semantics while improving streaming stability during function/tool handoffs. This PR introduces a lightweight "output contract negotiator" that reconciles parameter aliases (role, name, role_hints), stop array semantics and logprob shapes, and ensures a deterministic shape for framed streaming messages so downstream SDKs and proxies can rely on a single contract.

What changed (summary):
- Add a negotiator module that maps incoming /v1 parameters to our internal canonical form and emits an explicit output contract header for streams (used by adapters and SDKs).
- Implement an fncall handoff buffer for streaming: when a function/tool call is emitted mid-stream we pause token emission, flush partial deltas, and send a durable handshake event so consumers can resume parsing without dropped tokens. Buffering includes a small heartbeat to avoid client timeouts.
- Normalize stop/list semantics and logprob envelope: stop arrays are coerced to deterministic token sentinel lists and logprobs follow a stable shape even when truncated by batching.
- Backcompat: preserve older role aliases and provide fallbacks if enum variants are missing from clients.
- Tests: end-to-end adapter integration tests, unit tests for negotiator mappings, and new streaming fuzz cases included.

Checklist:
- [x] API mapping module implemented and covered by unit tests
- [x] Streaming handshake protocol for fncall buffering implemented and tested
- [x] Adapter changes applied to v1/chat path and verified in e2e tests
- [x] Docs/migration notes added for SDKs

Notes on risk and rollout: This change is additive and guarded behind the v1/chat adapter path. We emit a clear output_contract header for streams; older SDKs will ignore it. The fncall buffering introduces a small latency window (~4-10ms typical) on handoffs but prevents parser failures and dropped tokens, improving overall reliability for long-running tool interactions.

Related: ENG-2145 (streaming reliability), ENG-2199 (openai-compat param mapping).

release_notes: v1/chat: Add output contract negotiation for streaming parity with OpenAI, and introduce buffered fncall handoffs to avoid dropped tokens during tool calls. Includes stop/logprob normalization and SDK migration notes.
